status: Elementary derivations and experimental consequences; not new theorems

items.claim: Self-generated D is additional computation, not an independent spatial observation.
items.assumptions: Fixed theta; given X, D uses randomness independent of hidden scene truth Z; no new sensor/tool/retrieval result between X and D.
items.meaning: No impossibility of bounded-compute benefit follows. D can reorganize computation. If a tool is queried, its evidence and cost must be included in all appropriate controls.

items.claim: Teacher-conditioned evaluation does not establish deployed policy utility.
items.assumptions: Fix state/request x and the same action kernel p(A|x,d). Let q(d|x) be the teacher-decision distribution on that input and r(d|x) the deployed generated-decision distribution. For downstream utility U(A,x) in [0,1], define g(d)=E[U(A,x)|x,d].
items.derivation: |E_q g-E_r g| <= TV(q,r), because 0<=g<=1. On a finite support, write signed q-r as positive and negative parts, each with mass TV; maximizing the bounded expectation difference selects the positive part.
items.meaning: An oracle-rationale score can differ substantially from self-generated deployment. No small TV, no guarantee. Our data does not estimate this TV; the inequality is an elementary analysis, not a new result. Teacher annotation that saw A can make oracle action accuracy particularly easy.

items.claim: Training conditioned and unconditioned paths does not imply equal compute.
items.derivation: For conditioned execution p(A|X)=sum_D p(D|X)p(A|X,D). Greedy D followed by greedy A need not maximize that marginal. Two sequential calls and a longer action prefix consume additional prefill/decode compute.
items.meaning: Compare fixed-supervision and cost-quality experiments separately. Never count only A tokens or exclude invalid D calls.

items.claim: A common geometric preview proves only the predicates it computes.
items.derivation: If a preview computes C(T(S,A)) exactly for its own transition and predicates C, it can reject C-violations before execution. It says nothing about unmodeled semantics, path feasibility or errors in T/C.
items.meaning: The prior ordinary-search result supports explicit endpoint constraints on procedural boxes only. It neither validates all native execution noise nor makes a complete-room certificate.

items.claim: Furniture-stage supervision can support a full-generation contribution without training every stage.
items.derivation: Hold the other generation stages and resources common, replace only furniture policy, then compare final room outcomes under paired independent tasks.
items.meaning: This is a valid experimental design, not evidence already obtained. Scoring only furniture-stage endpoints would establish a narrower result.
